rec.name: PDP Animated Time Indicator (Progress Ring Counter)
rec.status: Built — code delivered by dev (ed-pdp-time-indicator.liquid), product image added for the example; no launch or test result recorded

what.text: A PDP section that shows 1–3 time-based key figures (e.g. setup time 25 Min, delivery time 48 Hours, return time 72 Hours) as large numbers inside circular progress rings. When the section scrolls into view, the number counts up from 0 to its target value while a coloured arc around it fills in sync. Each tile has a unit label (Min / Hours / Sec) inside the ring and a bold headline below it (e.g. 'Average setup time'). The section is centred on all viewports.

why.text: Concrete numbers make a product's promise tangible and quantifiable. A statement like 'assembles in 25 minutes' lowers perceived effort and risk, which are common objections for bulky products such as office chairs. Fast delivery and easy returns reduce purchase anxiety. The count-up and ring animation catches the eye, helps the figures stick, and makes the facts look like a credible, scannable 'dashboard' rather than marketing copy.

how.text: 1) Create a new theme section file 'ed-pdp-time-indicator.liquid' and paste in the delivered code (CSS, markup, JS and schema). The section appears in the theme editor as 'PDP | Time Indicator'. 2) Add it to the product template and add one 'Item' block per figure, up to 3 per the ticket. 3) For each block set the time value, unit and richtext headline, plus the ring colours, background and border colour. 4) Set section-level options: card size, gaps, ring width, content direction (unit below or beside the number), font sizes and spacing, with separate mobile values. Under the hood, each tile is an SVG with two circles (a track and an active arc). An IntersectionObserver at 50% visibility triggers a one-off setInterval count-up (about 1.2 s). It increments the number and animates stroke-dashoffset at the same time. An 'animated' class and a data-initialized flag stop it re-running. The code also re-initialises on Shopify theme-editor section/block events. Tiles sit in a centred flex-wrap row, so they stack on mobile.

items: Per block (Item): time value (text, e.g. 25)
Per block: unit text (e.g. Min, Hours)
Per block: richtext headline (bold / italic / underline possible)
Per block: ring colour, active/progress arc colour, text colour, inner circle background, border/fill colour
Section: text colour and background colour (transparent = fall back to theme colours)
Section: optional custom max-width (200–2500 px)
Section: spacing top/bottom/left/right (desktop and mobile)
Card (ring) size: 140–300 px desktop, separate mobile value (default 250 / 200)
Gap between cards (rem), desktop and mobile
Ring width 1–10, desktop and mobile
Inner content width (30–90%) and content direction (Row = unit beside number / Column = unit below)
Gap between number and unit
Font sizes for number, unit and headline, desktop and mobile
Tiles: 1–3 per the ticket (set by the number of Item blocks)

dependencies.text: No metafields or apps needed. Requires a Shopify Online Store 2.0 theme with a product template that accepts sections, and a '.container' wrapper class. Relies on theme global settings 'settings.text_color' and 'settings.background' as colour fallbacks. Font and number colour come from the theme settings. Browser needs IntersectionObserver support. The time value is parsed as an integer, and the ring is drawn as a percentage of 100, so a value of 25 fills 25% of the circle and a value above 100 would overflow the ring. Values in different units (e.g. 25 Min vs 72 Hours) therefore show different fill lengths that are not comparable to each other. The shipped code does not by itself enforce the 1–3 tile limit (the schema excerpt provided is cut off), so verify max_blocks in the final schema.

items: PDP conversion rate
Add-to-cart rate
Scroll depth / section view rate
PDP bounce and exit rate
Pre-sales support tickets about assembly, delivery and returns
Return rate (if setup effort or return expectations are better set)
